newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SEP eyes Singapore Telecom's Swedish Star TV.
newsitem.headline: SEP eyes Singapore Telecom's Swedish Star TV.

text.p: Swedish venture capital company Scandinavian Equity Partners (SEP) said on Wednesday it was interested in buying cable television company Star TV in Sweden from Singapore Telecom but would not say if a deal had been reached.
"I cannot comment more than saying we are still interested in Star TV," Nils Ingvar Lundin, spokesman for Swedish investment company Investor AB told Reuters.
SEP is owned by Investor, S-E-Banken, and U.S. investment group AEA Investors.
Swedish business daily Dagens Industri said Swedish telecoms company Netcom, part of the Kinnevik business sphere, was also interested in Star TV and had a verbal agreement to buy it.
Star TV, or Stjarn TV in Swedish, reaches around 230,000 Stockholm homes and is probably worth between 500 million and one billion crowns, Dagens Industri said.
The city of Stockholm sold Star TV to Singapore Telecom a number a years ago with a clause that it had the right to approve any future buyer of the television company, the newspaper said.
